narr: Thunderstorms moved northward through Pima and Cochise counties and produced heavy rainfall with reported totals ranging from 0.10 to 1.0 inches. The heavy rainfall closed multiple roadways in Tucson, Saint David, Tombstone, and Sierra Vista.
ev: Heavy rainfall closed from North of Wiley Road on Calle Riconado to South Wentworth Road due to flooding. Flooding occurred within the the Missile Tank Basin of Pima County.
Cochise County Sherriff reported flash flooding along East Madera Road in Sierra Vista resulting in a road closure. The road reopened at 9am on July 23rd.
Cochise County Official reported that Ghost Town Trail Road closed temporarily due to extensive flooding damage between mile post 2.8 and 13.

Cochise County Sherriff reported flash flooding along North Moson Road resulting in the entire road being closed between Charleston Road and Highway 90 in Sierra Vista. Photo showed at least a foot of fast moving water flowing over the roadway.
Cochise County reported Kings Highway closed at milepost 5.1 due to flooding. Unknown reopen time.

Cochise County Public Health official reported extensive roadway flooding along Courtland Road in Elfrida, AZ.
Pima County DOT closed Wentworth Rd north of Speedway due to flash flooding of the Tanque Verde Wash between Speedway and Redington Rd. The road was closed from 604pm to 743pm.
A trained spotter reported 3 feet of water moved through a narrow wash that crosses South Miller Lane near Highway 80 in St David AZ.
